title: Career roadmap · Startup Founder
summary: Build interdisciplinary research depth into a defensible technology or science venture through problem selection, validation, intellectual property, fundraising, regulatory planning and commercial execution.

facts.Current degree: D.Sc / D.Litt / DBA / Post-Doctoral & Industry-Sponsored Doctorates
facts.Course: Interdisciplinary Ph.D. (Data Science, Sustainability, Public Health, Cognitive Science, Bioengineering, Energy)
facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap treats 2026 as the starting point for converting advanced research into a venture. The objective is not to create a company immediately; it is to identify a technically defensible problem, validate demand, establish ownership of the relevant IP, build a credible founding team and progress from research prototype to sustainable business.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Research-to-venture founder, technical co-founder, innovation fellow or venture-building researcher with a validated problem and early prototype.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Build a focused deep-tech, health-tech, climate-tech, AI/data or bioengineering company around a defensible research capability.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Move from founder-led experimentation to product, regulatory, commercial and organisational leadership.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Build a multi-product or platform company, pursue strategic partnerships and continue investing in frontier R&D.

rows.text: Identify 10 research-derived problems and interview at least 20 potential users/stakeholders
Produce a validated-problem report with interview evidence and a defined target user
Write a one-page business model and a measurable value proposition
Demonstrate a working prototype or validated technical proof-of-concept
Complete a prior-art search and documented IP strategy before public disclosure
Obtain documented pilot/customer commitments or equivalent validation
Relevant regulator; BIRAC for biotech/health innovation
Produce a regulatory map covering approvals, standards and evidence requirements
Prepare a pitch deck, financial model, data room and funding plan
Secure first paying customer, pilot revenue or equivalent independently verified traction
Establish hiring, finance, IP, compliance and product-development processes

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Preserve a strong technical moat while building capabilities in sales, finance, hiring, regulatory strategy and organisational design. The founder's role should progressively shift from proving the technology to allocating capital and talent toward the highest-value opportunities.
At this stage, conventional internships are less important than incubation, venture-building programmes, research commercialisation and industry pilots.

blocks.label: Live-posting note
blocks.text: Founder roles are not normally “hired” positions. Build a parallel employability route—such as Research Scientist or R&D Lead—so that the student can develop industry experience and optionality while validating the venture.
For this pathway, another general degree is usually less useful than postdoctoral research, incubation, sponsored R&D and commercialisation programmes.

blocks.label: Typical years
blocks.text:
2026–2030 → research-to-venture validation
2030–2035 → founder/product-market development
2035–2040 → company and R&D leadership
2040–2046 → portfolio innovation/serial entrepreneurship
Ph.D./research routes

The founder's advantage should remain the ability to connect frontier research with a real problem. Maintain an active research pipeline, protect strategically important IP, develop partnerships with universities and industry, and build an organisation capable of funding long-horizon R&D without depending entirely on the founder's personal technical contribution.
